slides.title: Why pytest? 🧪
slides.content:
# No Boilerplate 🚫

Unlike traditional `unittest` (which requires classes), pytest uses plain functions.

## Basic Test
Create a file named `test_sample.py`.
```pytest
def func(x):
    return x + 1

def test_answer():
    assert func(3) == 5
```
Run it with `pytest` command. It will fail (4 != 5) and show a detailed diff.

Parametrization
slides.content:
# DRY Testing 🔁

Run the same test with different inputs.

```pytest
@pytest.mark.parametrize("input,expected", [
    (1, 2),
    (2, 3),
    (10, 11),
])
def test_increment(input, expected):
    assert input + 1 == expected
```
